Dushparājaya, a son of Dhṛtarāshṭra. § 182 (Dhṛtarāshṭraputranāmak.): I, 117, 4548.

Dushpradharsha, a son of Dhṛtarāshṭra. § 581 (Bhīshmavadhap.): VI, 64, 2838 (among fourteen sons of Dhṛtarāshṭra, who attacked Bhīmasena).--§ 608 (Karṇap.): VIII, 51, 2447.--§ 611 (Śalyap.): IX, 26, 1405 (attacked Bhīmasena), 1418 (is slain by Bhīmasena). Cf. next.

Dushpradharshaṇa, a son of Dhṛtarāshṭra. § 130 (Aṃśāvat.): I, 67, 2729.--§ 182 (Dhṛtarāshṭraputranāmak.): I, 117, 4542.--§ 232 (Svayaṃvarap.): I, 186, 6981 (came to the svayaṃvara of Draupadī).--§ 600 (Ghaṭotkacavadhap.): VII, 170, 7671. Cf. next.
Dushpraharsha, a son of Dhṛtarāshṭra. § 130 (Aṃśāvat.): I, 67, 2731.

Dushyanta^1, an ancient king, the husband of Śakuntalā and the father of Bharata. § 11 (Parvasaṅgr.): I, 2, 371 (C. Dushmantāt).--§ 133: The founder of the Paurava line was D., who ruled the whole world, even the Mlecchas. Description of his happy rule. D. could take up the mountain Mandara and support it in his arms (I, 68). One day D. went a hunting (I, 69). Having come to a forest, which was situated near the river Mālinī and was the resort of ascetics, Cāraṇas, Gandharvas, Apsarases, monkeys, Vālakhilyas, etc. (I, 70), D., in the hermitage of the Ṛshi Kaṇva Kāśyapa, saw Kaṇva's adopted daughter Śakuntalā: I, 68, 2801 (Pauravānāṃ vaṃśakaraḥ); 69, 2815, 2833, 2834; 71, 2898, 2909.--§ 134 (Viśvāmitra): I, 71, (2910).--§ 135 (Śakuntalop.): I, 73, (2955), (2960), 2970, 2981, 2985, 2987; 74, 3001, 3023, (3060), 3070, 3100, 3101, 3102, 3104, 3113, 3117 (rājarshiḥ; D. wedded Śakuntalā according to the Gāndharva form of marriage and returned to his capital. Śakuntalā brought her son Bharata to D., who did not at first acknowledge him as his son, until a celestial voice corroborated the truth of Śakuntalā's words).--§ 150 (Pūruvaṃś.): I, 94, 3707 (son of Īlina), 3708, 3709 (father of Bharata).--§ 156 (do.): I, 95, ††3781 (son of Īlina), ††3782 (married to Śakuntalā), 3783 (father of Bharata).-§ 267 (Yamasabhāv.): II, 8, 326 (in the palace of Yama).-§ 565 (Gālavacarita): V, 117, 3974 (reme…yathā… Śakuntalāyāṃ Dºḥ, C. Dushvº).--§ 761 (Ānuśāsanik.): XIII, 115, 5666 (among the kings who did not eat meat during the month of Kārttika; C. has Dushmantaḥ).--§ 775 (do.): XIII, 166, 7676.
Dushyanta^2, son of Ajamīḍha. § 152 (Pūruvaṃś.): I, 94, 3722 (D. and Parameshṭhin were the sons of Ajamīḍha with Nīlī), 3723 (the offspring of D. and Parameshṭhin were all the Pāñcālas).
